No significant group differences were found for the frontal, limbic, and temporal lobes, whereas LTAA had significantly lower gray matter volumes than NAC for the occipital and parietal lobes and the insula.

Within the occipital lobe, LTAA had less gray matter than NAC in the visual association area and primary visual cortex; within the parietal lobe, the lateral and mesial parietal areas exhibited reduced gray matter volumes in LTAA.
These findings indicate regionally specific persistent gray matter deficits in LTAA, particularly parietal lobe shrinkage consistent with spatial processing deficits.
